title: Internal structure of exotic hadrons
bottleneck: Experiments have confirmed pentaquarks and tetraquarks, yet it is unknown whether these exotic hadrons are compact multi-quark states or loosely bound molecules of ordinary hadrons. Different models predict different spectra and decays, and current data cannot decisively discriminate.
why_it_blocks: Exotic hadrons are QCD's laboratory for how confinement organizes multiquark systems; misidentifying their structure means misunderstanding the strong force's binding rules.
current_state: LHCb continues discovering new exotics with growing precision, and lattice QCD is beginning to compute their properties, but the compact-versus-molecular debate remains open for most states. Lattice QCD calculations of tetraquark binding energies are steadily improving, but distinguishing compact multi-quark states from hadronic molecules requires precision not yet achieved. Decay patterns and production rates offer complementary handles that LHCb continues to refine.
